questions.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{5{y}^{2}}{4{z}^{2}}\cdot \frac{8xz}{y}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we cancel any terms that appear in both a numerator and a denominator. Then, we multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5{y}^{2}}{4{z}^{2}}\cdot \frac{8xz}{y} & =\frac{5y\cdot y}{4z\cdot z}\cdot \frac{4z\cdot 2x}{y} \\  & =\frac{5y\cdot \cancel{y}}{\cancel{4z}\cdot z}\cdot \frac{\cancel{4z}\cdot 2x}{\cancel{y}} \\  & =\frac{5y}{z}\cdot \frac{2x}{1} \\  & =\frac{10xy}{z}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $\frac{mn-4n}{2m}=a$ and $\frac{2}{m-4}=b$, what is $a\cdot b?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we factor all of the expressions and cancel any terms that appear in both a numerator and a denominator. Then, we multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =\frac{mn-4n}{2m}\cdot \frac{2}{m-4} \\  & =\frac{n(m-4)}{2\cdot m}\cdot \frac{2}{m-4} \\  & =\frac{n\cancel{(m-4)}}{\cancel{2}\cdot m}\cdot \frac{\cancel{2}}{\cancel{m-4}} \\  & =\frac{n}{m}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{{x}^{2}-16}{{x}^{2}-5x+6}\cdot \frac{x-3}{x-4}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we factor all of the expressions and cancel any terms that appear in both a numerator and a denominator. Then, we multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}-16}{{x}^{2}-5x+6}\cdot \frac{x-3}{x-4} & =\frac{(x+4)(x-4)}{(x-2)(x-3)}\cdot \frac{x-3}{x-4} \\  & =\frac{(x+4)\cancel{(x-4)}}{(x-2)\cancel{(x-3)}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{(x-3)}}{\cancel{x-4}} \\  & =\frac{x+4}{x-2}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Given that $\dfrac {6a} {b^2} = x$ and $\dfrac {3b} {2a}= y,$ what is $x\cdot y?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot y & =\frac{6a}{{b}^{2}}\cdot \frac{3b}{2a} \\  & =\frac{6a\cdot 3b}{{b}^{2}\cdot 2a} \\  & =\frac{18ab}{2a{b}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{9}{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** In the above example, we performed some cancellations after multiplying. However, with more complex expressions, it's often easier to cancel *before* multiplying.

$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Multiplying rational expressions is just like multiplying fractions. After all, fractions are just rational expressions with constants!

For example, to multiply the rational expressions $\dfrac{3}{x}$ and $\dfrac{y}{2},$ we multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

$$
\dfrac{3}{x} \cdot \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{3 \cdot y}{x \cdot 2} = \dfrac{3y}{2x}
$$
